title: HiRISE
desc: Camera that views very small objects. Expensive, heavy, high energy usage; must shut down during dust storms to keep the battery alive.

title: Context Camera
desc: Provides a background view of Martian terrain. Expensive, very heavy, high energy usage; must shut down during dust storms to keep the battery alive.

title: Mars Colour Imager
desc: Produces a climate overview of Mars and spots weather problems, but suffers from low resolution.

title: CRISM Spectrometer
desc: Searches for mineral residue. High energy usage; must shut down during dust storms to keep the battery alive.

title: MCS
desc: Measures temperature, humidity, and dust content, though it is vulnerable to radiation damage.

title: SHARAD
desc: Detects underground liquid and frozen substances. Support arms may jam when unfolded, hindering satellite balance.

title: UHF Comms Package
desc: Handles navigation and communications with Earth. Outdated hardware with low-PR images, though it offers broad visibility.

title: Optical Nav Camera
desc: Pinpoints spacecraft trajectory with high accuracy, but uses a fixed mount with no backups.

title: Ka-band Telecom
desc: Fast communications with Earth, though its thin beam is heavily absorbed by clouds.

title: Solar Electric Propulsion
desc: Uses ion thrusters with less mass, though it takes a longer route to Mars and increases mission time.

title: Rideshare on Separate Mission
desc: Attaches the orbiter to a separate Mars mission to save fuel. Faces strict weight/size limits and potential launch delays.

title: Dedicated Chemical Propulsion
desc: Provides direct, fast course corrections and controlled orbital insertion, but is expensive and very heavy.

title: Extra Testing and Backups
desc: Adds redundancy and testing to prevent support arm jams, though it doubles the cost.

title: Strip Out Backup Parts
desc: Cuts costs by removing backup parts, resulting in a high chance of jams or component failure.

title: Lighter Passive Sensor
desc: Saves weight and money, but cannot see deep underground water.

title: Dust Clearing Solar Panels
desc: Keeps power generation active during dust storms, though it is expensive and adds complexity.

title: Aerogel Insulation
desc: Uses low-temperature hardware with insulation so no heaters are required, reducing off-the-shelf instrument use.

title: AI Data Compression
desc: Software compresses shots before sending to Earth to prevent data gridlock, carrying a risk of software bugs.

title: Offload Earth Transmission
desc: Relays data through an existing Mars orbiter, though bandwidth is heavily rationed.

title: Dedicated Antenna
desc: Focuses the signal, but is heavy, high-power, expensive, and must compete with other missions for Deep Space Network tracking time.

title: Budget Weather Context Orbiter
desc: Low resolution imagery that cannot identify safe landing zones.

title: Multiple Mid-Tier Instruments
desc: Uses multiple mid-tier instruments, but cannot spot dangerous rocks at landing sites.

title: Relay Orbiter
desc: Combines high-resolution imaging and relay comms to spot safe landing zones, though it is expensive and uses high power.
